events.description: Sharaa's coalition ousted Bashar al-Assad; Sharaa appointed himself president.
Sharaa visited Washington/the White House ('just the other day'); met members of Congress; filmed playing basketball with CENTCOM commander Adm. Cooper.
Syria agreed a limited, conditional membership of the anti-ISIS coalition; nothing on peace with Israel or enforceable minority guarantees.
Massacre of Alawites in Latakia; Reuters investigation found Sharaa's people including his defense ministry ordered and directed it; no one punished.
Massacre of Druze by members of Sharaa's coalition; second massacre in his first eight months.
UN resolution lifting sanctions on Sharaa and his former deputy passed; China abstained.
Six-month extension of the suspension of US sanctions on Syria; sanctions not yet gone.
Jolani's dispute with Baghdadi over control of the Syrian jihad (2013-14) split the movement; Zawahiri ejected the Islamic State and sided with Jolani.
US unofficially served as the Taliban's air force against the Islamic State in Nangarhar and surrounding provinces, c. 2015-2019.
Within two years of the end of US-Taliban anti-ISIS cooperation the Taliban walked into Kabul.
Interviewed about 9/11, Sharaa said he was only 19 and that it was sad innocent people died; refused to denounce it.
Sharaa said it is premature to seek a peace agreement with Israel.
Mohammed bin Salman due in Washington 'next week' to meet Trump; Syria on the agenda.
Sharaa appointed foreign fighters, including a TIP division, into the Syrian military.

key_claims: Sharaa (Jolani) is a former — and possibly current — al-Qaeda leader whose 'break' with al-Qaeda was a distancing approved by al-Qaeda leaders; key members of his government are designated al-Qaeda figures.
Sharaa's White House visit extracted almost nothing: partial anti-ISIS coalition membership, no peace with Israel, no enforceable minority guarantees.
Two massacres (Alawites in Latakia, Druze) in Sharaa's first eight months; the Latakia killings were directed from his defense ministry per Reuters.
Backing one jihadist strain to suppress another (Taliban vs ISIS, Sharaa vs ISIS) is a repeated error; the US acted as the Taliban's air force 2015-19 and the Taliban took Kabul two years later.
Unlike Hibatullah, who never engages infidels, Sharaa can be held accountable by phone — Fitton-Brown argues for 'engage, don't trust, verify'.
Assad's fall is Iran's biggest blow in two years, cutting its route to Hezbollah and the Iraqi militias' Syrian training ground.
TIP's thousands of fighters sit inside the Syrian army and report to an Afghanistan-based leader on al-Qaeda's executive shura.
The Taliban have comprehensively broken their Doha promise by backing TTP and al-Qaeda cross-border operations into Pakistan.
Roggio: the Syrian civil war has not ended; Sharaa only transitioned it to its next phase.
